title: A Portrait for the Room
premise: Theo Iversen returns to the coastal town of Greywater to bury his twin brother Elias, only to discover the body in the coffin has Elias's face and someone else's fingerprints. The town's founding families have kept a bargain for two centuries, feeding a presence beneath the meetinghouse in exchange for prosperity, and Elias died trying to end it. When Theo's grief-driven sleep recordings capture a second voice — Elias's voice — answering questions no one asked aloud, Theo is dragged into the founders' ritual as the required final bloodline. To honor his brother, he must complete the ritual the founders corrupted: not to feed the thing below, but to name it, judge it, and let it starve — a verdict rendered outside any court, at the cost of Theo's own memory of Elias.
about_author: Noor Voss is the pen name of a former court stenographer from the Pacific Northwest who spent eleven years transcribing verdicts before turning to fiction. Their work explores what justice looks like when the law refuses to look at all.

chapters.title: The Wrong Brother
chapters.summary: Theo arrives in Greywater for the funeral and insists on viewing the body, a habit of a skeptic who trusts nothing secondhand. In the casket he finds his twin's face — and a stranger's scarred hands. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion; the first crack in his unbelief.

chapters.title: Household of One
chapters.summary: Theo stays in Elias's house against the advice of the town registrar, Maren Kolve, who warns him some rooms should be sold as-is. He finds Elias's notebooks: dates, names, and a column labeled simply 'owed.' POV: Theo. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Founders' Pew
chapters.summary: At the memorial service, Theo watches the five founding families occupy the front pews and notice who does not grieve. Old Halvard Brandt presses a coin into Theo's palm — payment, he says, for services his family has always rendered. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the sense of being claimed.

chapters.title: Sleep, Recorded
chapters.summary: Unable to rest, Theo plays the white-noise recordings Elias left running every night. On night three, beneath his own breathing, a second voice answers questions Theo never asked. The voice says his name. POV: Theo, with transcript interludes. Emotional beat: terror of being overheard by something patient.

chapters.title: What Elias Owed
chapters.summary: Following the notebooks, Theo learns Elias spent his last year interviewing descendants of the town's 'unrecorded' dead — the poor, the shipped-in, the disappeared who fed the founders' bargain. POV: Theo, with Elias's journal entries. Emotional beat: brotherhood redefined as inheritance.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren Kolve, registrar and reluctant keeper of the founding charters, shows Theo the original covenant: prosperity in perpetuity, in exchange for a named bloodline every generation. Her own name is on the debtor's side. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: complicity and its quiet rot.

chapters.title: The Meetinghouse Below
chapters.summary: Theo breaks into the meetinghouse cellar and finds the founders' ritual chamber — a circle of chairs facing a sealed well, each chair engraved with a family name. The seventh chair is blank. Elias's coat hangs on it. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dread made architectural.

chapters.title: The Voice Names Itself
chapters.summary: The recording voice grows conversational, answering Theo's questions in Elias's cadence but not his knowledge. It claims to be what the founders fed — and claims Elias is not gone but 'held.' Theo must decide whether comfort can lie. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the seduction of false reunion.

chapters.title: Halvard's Bargain
chapters.summary: Halvard Brandt offers Theo the family fortune to sit the seventh chair willingly at the equinox, insisting the ritual is mercy, not murder. He shows Theo what Greywater was before: a starving village that made a deal. POV: Halvard. Emotional beat: horror with a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Unrecorded
chapters.summary: Theo meets the descendants Elias interviewed, living at the town's margins. They keep their own counter-ledger of names the founders erased. One, a woman named Sef, recognizes Theo's face and grieves it — she knew Elias. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: solidarity among the uncounted.

chapters.title: Interference
chapters.summary: The founders move against the investigation: Elias's house is searched, his notebooks stolen, Sef's workshop burned. Theo realizes the recordings are the only evidence left — and the voice in them begins editing itself. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the ground giving way.

chapters.title: What the Well Wants
chapters.summary: In a trance-adjacent night, the voice explains its nature: it does not demand sacrifice; it only keeps what is given, and the founders have spent two centuries teaching it appetite. Elias tried to starve it and was 'collected' as interest. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: pity for the monster, hatred for its keepers.

chapters.title: The Registrar's Confession
chapters.summary: Maren admits her family has signed every renewal, including the one due at this equinox — with Theo's name now in the blank. She offers him the charter's one flaw: a verdict clause the founders never dared invoke. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: guilt converted into courage.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Theo, Sef, and Maren reconstruct Elias's plan: the ritual's original form was a trial — the entity named, its debts itemized, its keepers' consent withdrawn. But the rite requires a bloodline to stand as both accuser and surety. Theo volunteers. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: resolve with a counted cost.

chapters.title: The Founder's Doubt
chapters.summary: Halvard's daughter, Ines, defects, revealing the founders' secret: the last verdict attempt, in 1893, failed because the accuser flinched and was consumed. She gives Theo the 1893 transcript — her family's shame, preserved. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: inherited guilt seeking discharge.

chapters.title: The Voice's Offer
chapters.summary: The entity, sensing the plan, changes tactics: it offers Elias back — truly back, it claims — if Theo sits the chair as feeder instead of judge. It speaks with Elias's childhood memories. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the cruelest temptation; grief weaponized.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: The town prepares its founding festival, oblivious above the sealed well. The founders detain Maren, burn the counter-ledger's last copy, and seal Theo's exits. Sef smuggles him the recovered recordings. POV: Sef. Emotional beat: the machinery of power closing in.

chapters.title: The Seventh Chair
chapters.summary: Theo descends to the chamber under founder escort, sits, and instead of consenting, opens the trial: he names the entity, itemizes two centuries of the fed, and reads the founders' own covenant as a confession. The well begins to answer. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into authority.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: The entity, given voice, does not defend itself — it only asks who will hold what it holds. Theo accepts surety: every name, every debt, every memory of Elias passes through him to be witnessed and released. The founders' chairs crack as their claim is voided. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: judgment as sacrifice; the price made flesh.

chapters.title: Starving the Well
chapters.summary: With consent withdrawn and debts discharged, the entity thins to silence — not banished, simply no longer fed. Elias's presence fades last, and the voice thanks his brother in words that are finally only Elias's own. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: farewell without resurrection.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Recorded
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Greywater's prosperity visibly decays, and the founders scatter or face the town's new reckoning — a citizens' tribunal Maren convenes from the counter-ledger's surviving fragments. Theo testifies, then resigns the case. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: justice continued by ordinary hands.

chapters.title: A Portrait for the Room
chapters.summary: Theo commissions a portrait of Elias from Sef and hangs it in the house — then burns his last sleep recordings unplayed, choosing memory over evidence. The blank seventh chair stays in the cellar, empty on purpose. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: survival priced and paid; grief kept, haunting released.
